const source = ref<string | null>("a");
const value = computed(() => source.value);

</script>

<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, provide, ref, reactive, readonly } from 'vue';
import type { Ref } from 'vue';
import MyChild from './components/MyChild.vue';
import { CastKey, PlainKey } from './composables/keys';
const source = ref('a');
const value = computed(() => source.value);
const state = reactive({ count: 1 });
const plainValue = 'a';
const snapshot = source.value;
function getValue() { return 'a'; }
function useService() { return { value: source }; }
provide(PlainKey, value);
provide(CastKey, value);
</script>

<template>
  <MyChild />
</template>

messages.help:
WARNING vize:croquis/cf/non-reactive-provide
provide('CastKey') value is not reactive - consumers won't see updates
Problem: provide('CastKey', value) passes a plain value to consumers.
Why this matters:
- Consumers that call inject() receive a snapshot-like value.
- Later provider updates will not be visible unless consumers receive a ref or computed value.
Safer patterns:

  provide('CastKey', ref(value))
  provide('CastKey', computed(() => value))
Suggestion: provide('key', ref(value)) or provide('key', computed(() => value))

Suggestion: Store inject result first: const (destructured) = inject(CastKey), then access properties

provide('CastKey') value is not reactive - consumers won't see updates
Problem: provide('CastKey', value) passes a plain value to consumers.
Why this matters:
- Consumers that call inject() receive a snapshot-like value.
- Later provider updates will not be visible unless consumers receive a ref or computed value.
Safer patterns:

  provide('CastKey', ref(value))
  provide('CastKey', computed(() => value))
Suggestion: provide('key', ref(value)) or provide('key', computed(() => value))
